commanderCards.oracleText:
Islandwalk, swampwalk (This creature can't be blocked as long as defending player controls an Island or a Swamp.)
Whenever Wrexial deals combat damage to a player, you may cast target instant or sorcery card from that player's graveyard without paying its mana cost. If that spell would be put into a graveyard, exile it instead.

strategy: Build Wrexial as optimized Dimir control-combo: use efficient interaction and premium draw engines to establish control, then exploit stocked opposing graveyards through Wrexial. Replace expensive theft and standalone mill with wheel disruption, compact Mindcrank finishes, and Hullbreaker Horror mana loops, retaining Exsanguinate and Blue Sun's Zenith as outlets. This pushes power within the supplied Bracket 4 rules and the 15-swap limit; reserve wins and game-ending wheel locks for turn four or later rather than pursuing an early cEDH race.

swaps.reason: Four-mana flash disruption is substantially more practical than a ten-mana threat. With Windfall or Whispering Madness, it denies opposing draws while their discarded spells supply Wrexial.

research.summary:
## 1. Main strategies/archetypes

Current EDHREC data and published decklists point to three overlapping approaches—not one settled “best” build: ([edhrec.com](https://edhrec.com/commanders/wrexial-the-risen-deep))

- **Mill into spell theft/control:** Fill opposing graveyards, connect with **Wrexial, the Risen Deep**, and cast their best instants/sorceries. Mill can supply resources rather than be the primary win condition. ([tappedout.net](https://tappedout.net/mtg-decks/12-11-19-wrexial-the-risen-deep/))
- **Dedicated mill/combo:** Use repeatable mill and library-halving effects, with **Duskmantle Guildmage**, **Bruvac the Grandiloquent**, or **Fraying Sanity** as finishers. ([edhrec.com](https://edhrec.com/commanders/wrexial-the-risen-deep/mill))
- **Graveyard theft/reanimator, sometimes with discard:** Exploit milled creatures as well as spells. **Sea-monster/landwalk** builds are another recognizable branch; **Gyruda, Doom of Depths** companion builds are a smaller niche. ([edhrec.com](https://edhrec.com/commanders/wrexial-the-risen-deep))

## 2. Key synergy cards and engines

| Role | Specific cards and purpose |
|---|---|
| **Stock graveyards** | **Ruin Crab**, **Fractured Sanity**, **Maddening Cacophony**, **Nemesis of Reason**, **Consuming Aberration**. The last two provide repeatable mill rather than only a one-shot effect. |
| **Exploit those graveyards** | **Memory Plunder**, **Diluvian Primordial** for spell theft; **Extract from Darkness**, **Sepulchral Primordial**, **Geth, Lord of the Vault** for creature theft/reanimation. |
| **Graveyard payoffs/control** | **Drown in the Loch**, **Syr Konrad, the Grim**, **Lazav, Dimir Mastermind**, **Phenax, God of Deception**. |

These packages recur in EDHREC recommendations and actual Wrexial lists. ([edhrec.com](https://edhrec.com/commanders/wrexial-the-risen-deep/mill))

- **Make Wrexial connect:** **Spreading Seas**, **Sea's Claim**, **Quicksilver Fountain**, **Harbinger of the Seas**, and **Blanket of Night** enable landwalk. **Lightning Greaves** and **Swiftfoot Boots** help a six-mana commander survive and attack promptly. ([edhrec.com](https://edhrec.com/commanders/wrexial-the-risen-deep))
- **Sea-monster package:** **Whelming Wave** leaves Wrexial behind; **Stormtide Leviathan**, **Serpent of Yawning Depths**, and **Spawning Kraken** support evasive sea-monster combat. ([edhrec.com](https://edhrec.com/commanders/wrexial-the-risen-deep))

## 3. Popular combos—exact outputs

These appear on Wrexial’s EDHREC combo page; **none requires Wrexial himself**. ([edhrec.com](https://edhrec.com/combos/wrexial-the-risen-deep))

- **Duskmantle Guildmage + Mindcrank:** Activate the Guildmage’s first ability for **{1}{U}{B}**, then cause an opponent to lose life or put a card into their graveyard. Mill causes life loss, which causes more mill. **Result: a lethal life-loss/mill loop**, provided the opponent has enough cards to sustain it; seed each opponent to eliminate the table. ([commanderspellbook.com](https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/936-5069/))
- **Bruvac the Grandiloquent + Maddening Cacophony:** Cast **Maddening Cacophony** kicked, costing **{4}{U}{U}** total. Bruvac doubles the rounded-up half-library mill. **Result: every opponent mills their entire library**, absent replacement effects or other interference—not literally an infinite loop. ([commanderspellbook.com](https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/95-5080/))
- **Fraying Sanity + Maddening Cacophony:** A kicked Cacophony mills half of every opponent’s library; at the end step, **Fraying Sanity** mills the enchanted opponent’s remainder. **Result: one opponent’s library emptied**, with the others approximately halved. ([edhrec.com](https://edhrec.com/combos/mono-blue/464-5080))
- **Fraying Sanity + Traumatize:** **Result: the enchanted opponent mills their whole library if its starting size is even; ordinarily one card remains if odd**, unless another card entered their graveyard that turn. ([edhrec.com](https://edhrec.com/combos/mono-blue/464-781))

## 4. Common mistakes / underperformers

*These are interaction-based cautions and deckbuilding judgments, not a measured community “worst cards” ranking.*

- **The Mindskinner is a major nonbo:** It prevents your creatures’ damage to opponents, so Wrexial does **not** deal combat damage and does **not** trigger spell theft. It belongs in a committed mill plan, not automatically in a Wrexial-value deck. ([commanderspellbook.com](https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/648-6003/))
- **Too much small, single-opponent mill/discard:** **Glimpse the Unthinkable**, standalone **Traumatize**, and **Mind Rot** need sufficient payoffs; otherwise they spend cards without controlling the board. EDHREC’s discard article explicitly flags Mind Rot’s poor multiplayer scaling. ([edhrec.com](https://edhrec.com/articles/singleton-shmingleton-build-a-theft-deck-with-mind-rot))
- **Overloading expensive sea monsters:** My assessment: **Fleet Swallower** and **Stormtide Leviathan** are defensible themed finishers, but too many such cards compete with casting—and recasting—Wrexial. Keep early ramp and interaction intact. ([mtggoldfish.com](https://www.mtggoldfish.com/deck/7182936))

## 5. Mana base advice specific to Wrexial

- **Start around 36–38 lands**, then tune to curve and draw. Wrexial costs **{3}{U}{U}{B}**: prioritize reliable double blue. Use **Sol Ring**, **Arcane Signet**, **Dimir Signet**, and **Talisman of Dominance** to reach six mana earlier. This is a starting recommendation, consistent with sampled lists—not an optimized universal count. ([gatherer.wizards.com](https://gatherer.wizards.com/WWK/en-us/120/wrexial-the-risen-deep))
- **Fixing:** **Command Tower**, **Watery Grave**, **Morphic Pool**, **Underground River**, **Drowned Catacomb**, **Shipwreck Marsh**, and **Polluted Delta**; budget options include **Choked Estuary** and **Sunken Hollow** with adequate basics. ([edhrec.com](https://edhrec.com/commanders/wrexial-the-risen-deep/upgraded/expensive/average-deck))
- **Exceptional commander synergy:** **Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth** makes opponents’ lands Swamps, enabling Wrexial’s swampwalk while improving your black mana. ([commanderspellbook.com](https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/209-233-714/))
- **Build around your own land conversion:** **Harbinger of the Seas** also turns *your* nonbasic lands into Islands. Retain basic **Swamp** cards and artifact black sources; otherwise your evasion enabler can prevent you from casting Wrexial. ([gatherer.wizards.com](https://gatherer.wizards.com/MH3/en-us/63/harbinger-of-the-seas))

synergies.title: Unblockable, Immediate Wrexial
synergies.explanation: Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth makes every opponent's lands Swamps, enabling Wrexial's swampwalk against anyone who controls a land. Lightning Greaves adds haste and shroud, letting Wrexial attack immediately while protected from targeted removal.

synergies.title: Graveyards Become Your Toolbox
synergies.explanation: Dreamborn Muse stocks opponents' graveyards with spells for Wrexial and creatures for Animate Dead. Those growing graveyards also expand the range of spells and creatures Drown in the Loch can answer.

synergies.title: Cipher-Powered Hand Suppression
synergies.explanation: Encode Whispering Madness on Wrexial to turn his evasive combat hits into repeated wheels, while Narset, Parter of Veils limits each opponent to at most one card drawn that turn. The discarded cards stock future Wrexial attacks; newly discarded spells cannot become targets of a Wrexial trigger already on the stack.

synergies.title: Two Krakens, Twice the Theft
synergies.explanation: Sakashima the Impostor can copy Wrexial while retaining its own name, allowing both to coexist despite the legend rule. Each has islandwalk, swampwalk, and its own combat-damage spell-theft trigger.

synergies.title: Steal the Entire Windfall
synergies.explanation: With Notion Thief on the battlefield, Windfall discards everyone's hands but redirects all opponents' Windfall draws to you. This creates a massive hand advantage while filling opposing graveyards for Wrexial.

synergies.title: Combat and Drain Become Mill
synergies.explanation: Mindcrank turns Wrexial's combat damage into milling and makes Exsanguinate mill every opponent for the life they lose. This supplies more targets for future Wrexial triggers, while Exsanguinate also replenishes your life total.

synergies.title: Reusable Board Reset
synergies.explanation: After sacrificing Oblivion Stone to clear the board, Academy Ruins puts it back on top of your library for another use. If time and mana permit, a fate counter can preserve Wrexial through the destruction.

synergies.title: Recharge the Big Mana Rocks
synergies.explanation: Tezzeret the Seeker's +1 untaps Mana Vault and Basalt Monolith without paying their normal untap costs. Untapping both after tapping them produces another six colorless mana, accelerating Wrexial, expensive interaction, or a large Exsanguinate.

synergies.title: Multiply the Draw Engine
synergies.explanation: A kicked Rite of Replication targeting Consecrated Sphinx creates five additional Sphinxes. With the original still present, each card an opponent draws can yield twelve cards for you.

synergies.title: Upkeep Mill Becomes Life Drain
synergies.explanation: Once Bloodchief Ascension has three quest counters, every card Dreamborn Muse mills from an opponent can make that opponent lose 2 life and you gain 2 life. This turns the deck's graveyard-filling engine into a substantial multiplayer finisher without requiring an infinite combo.
